p.s: Every year, small businesses lose contracts they were fully qualified to win.
Not on price. Not on quality of work. On a technicality — a missing certificate, an insurance minimum that's a few thousand dollars short, a signature page nobody noticed was required.

Reading a dense RFP, checking it line by line against your own paperwork, and writing a tailored proposal can take hours — hours a business owner should be spending running the business, or bidding on the next contract.

This is BidWright — an agent built with the Strands Agents SDK that reads the RFP, checks your company against every requirement, drafts the proposal, and only asks you to decide the things only you can decide.
BidWright is built for the people who respond to RFPs regularly, but don't have a dedicated compliance team to do it:
municipal contractors, landscapers, janitorial and facilities companies, IT and managed-service providers, construction subcontractors — office managers and owners who are the entire back office.
What used to take an afternoon of cross-referencing now runs unattended.

And because the compliance check never claims something is met unless your own paperwork actually backs it up, you're not just saving time — you're not losing a winnable bid to a mistake you didn't catch.
Let's watch it work on a real example: a municipal landscaping RFP, and a small landscaping company's actual capability profile.

One click, and an orchestrator agent takes over — coordinating three specialized sub-agents, each returning validated, structured data instead of loose text one agent might hand the next and get wrong.

First, the RFP Analyzer reads the full solicitation and extracts a structured record: the submission deadline, required licenses and certifications, minimum insurance coverage, evaluation criteria, and a complete submission checklist.

Next, the Compliance Checker compares every single requirement against the company's actual profile — insurance certificates, licenses, staff qualifications — and marks each one met, gap, or needs review, with a severity and a concrete next step.

On this run, it correctly caught the company's general liability insurance sitting at one million dollars when the RFP requires two million per occurrence — along with a missing signed cover letter and a missing pricing schedule. Real gaps, precisely identified.

While that's happening, BidWright also writes a calendar reminder for the submission deadline — with automatic three-day and one-day advance warnings, so the deadline itself never becomes one more thing to track by hand.

Then the Proposal Drafter writes the actual proposal: cover letter, executive summary, technical approach, qualifications, and a compliance matrix — honestly flagging the open gaps instead of papering over them. Pricing is left to the owner; BidWright never invents numbers.
And everything funnels into exactly one place a busy owner actually needs to read: Decisions Needed.
One summary. Either "ready to submit," or here are the specific blocking gaps and what closes each one. Nothing else requires your attention unless you want to dig in.
BidWright drafts. It doesn't submit — a human always reviews and signs off, which is the entire point of that one summary.
Next up: broader document formats, more jurisdictions, and a verified deployment on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore for teams that want it running in the cloud, not just on a laptop.
BidWright — built with the Strands Agents SDK, for the Agents for Humans Hackathon. Read the RFP once. Draft with confidence.
